STAGE 3 · WHOLE SLIDE IMAGE (H&E)

Whole slide image → 64-d vector

The slide is cut into small tiles; the model learns which tiles matter most and combines them into a 64-number summary.

H&E-stained tissue, scanned at 40×
Attention heatmap over the same slide (paper Fig. 5B)

Step 1Whole slide image
We start from one tissue section of the tumour, stained with H&E and digitised at high resolution.
CaseTCGA-3C-AALI
StainHaematoxylin & eosin (H&E)
ScannerLeica SCN400, 40× magnification
Step 2Cut into tiles
The slide is divided into small square tiles (512 × 512 px at 40×).
Only tiles that contain tissue are used; empty glass is skipped.
Grid enlarged for visibility; the real tiles are smaller.
Step 3Describe each tile
Each tile is turned into 1,536 numbers by a pathology foundation model.
One tile from the slide
UNI2-h (pretrained, frozen)
pathology foundation model, not trained further
1,536 numbers per tile
Step 4Find important tiles
A Transformer compares all tiles; attention gives each tile an importance weight. The highest-weighted tiles fall on tumour-rich regions.
High
Low
Attention
Warm colours: tiles the model relies on most.
Cool colours: tiles it relies on least.
Heatmap: gated attention of the trained model (paper Fig. 5B).
Step 5Most important tiles
The six tiles with the highest attention weight (paper Fig. 5C).
1,024 tiles · top 100 tiles hold 12.2% of the attention · entropy 6.92 nats
Step 6Combine
All tiles are added up, each weighted by its importance, into one slide summary.
… 1,024 tiles
Σ
weighted sum of tiles + [CLS] summary, projected to 64 numbers
64-d vector (histopathology data)
STAGE 4 · COMBINING THE THREE DATA TYPES

Combining clinical, gene and slide information → ER, PR, HER2

The three 64-number summaries share information, then the network outputs a probability for each receptor.

S = [e(c); e(g); e(w)] → T = LN(MHA(S,S,S) + S) → f = vec(T) ∈ ℝ192 → trunk → heads → σ
